problem: Prior urban VLN agents (seq-to-seq LSTMs such as ORAR, and fine-tuned VL transformers) fuse image feature vectors and need full supervised training. It was also unclear how to connect a vision-less LLM to a long-horizon (~40 steps), large-scale, real-world Street View environment. In addition, the standard Touchdown environment auto-rotates the agent at intersections, so the correct action sequences are semantically misaligned with instructions like 'turn right at the intersection', which breaks few-shot agents.
motivation: LLMs reason well and have been used for household, game and indoor (NavGPT) agents. But urban VLN combines a huge real road graph, dense real panoramas, open-ended landmarks (store names, logos, vehicles) and trajectories about 7x longer than R2R, so captioning every view as NavGPT does is impractical. The observation driving the paper is that only the landmarks mentioned in the instruction matter, so checking just those with CLIP and verbalizing the result gives a compact text interface an LLM can act on.
key_idea: Embody a text-only LLM through verbalization: extract the instruction's landmarks with an LLM, detect their visibility in 5 view directions with standardized/thresholded CLIP scores, and append templated observation text ('There is a 4-way intersection', 'There is X on your slightly left') to a growing prompt. The next action is then chosen by next-word prediction.
insight: Verbalizing only the instruction-relevant visual evidence is enough for a blind LLM to navigate. 2-shot GPT-4 reaches 44%/77% of a fully trained ORAR's TC. Fine-tuned LLaMA-7B on verbalized observations beats vector-level image fusion (ORAR♠), which the authors attribute to text observations overfitting less in the geographically unseen split. The vision ablation (Table 3, VELMA-FT dev) shows landmark detection matters most on Touchdown: TC is 15.0 with no image model, 20.8 with CLIP ViT-L/14 and 23.4 with OpenCLIP bigG. On Map2seq the corresponding values are 37.8, 39.2 and 41.3, so gains track CLIP quality. Response-based learning adds +2.9/+7.5 test TC. It lets the agent learn from its own trajectories and credits any stop within one node; qualitatively it learns to walk past and turn_around when an 'overshoot' landmark appears. Few-shot KPA does not translate into TC for weaker LLMs: LLaMA-2 reaches 48.3/57.7 KPA but only 2.1/3.2 TC, and OPT-65B barely beats a forward-only heuristic.
method: Environment fix: modified Touchdown state transition with no auto-rotation after FORWARD. At intersections, left/forward/right are chosen as the left-most/middle/right-most outgoing edge, so action sequences align with instruction semantics. A TURN_AROUND action (heading −180°) is also added.

Landmark extractor: a 5-shot prompt to GPT-3, run once before navigation, lists the landmarks in each instruction (2.7 per instruction on average; F1 96.3 Touchdown / 99.6 Map2seq on 50 hand-annotated dev instances each; ~58% of test landmarks are novel).

Landmark scorer: OpenCLIP ViT-bigG-14 scores 'picture of [landmark]' against 800x460, 60° FoV views at −90/−45/0/+45/+90° (left/slightly left/ahead/slightly right/right). Scores are z-standardized per landmark using all views of ~20k training-area panoramas, and a landmark is visible if z > τ=3.5 (hand-picked, not tuned). Traffic-flow orientation is also predicted with front- vs rear-view-of-vehicle CLIP prompts at the start.

Verbalizer: template text for intersections (≥3 outgoing edges in nav graph → 'There is a N-way intersection') and visible landmarks ('There is [l] on your [m]'). The prompt is x_t = [task desc, instructions, o_1, 1, a_1, …, o_t, t], and the action is taken from LLM next-word probabilities over the 5 action literals.
Few-shot mode: frozen LLM (GPT-3, GPT-4, Mixtral, plus LLaMA/LLaMA-2/OPT/Mistral scaling study) with 2 in-context full gold-path text sequences from the training set.

VELMA-FT: LLaMA-7B with a LoRA adapter (r=8, alpha=16, dropout 0.05), fine-tuned by teacher forcing on gold-path verbalized sequences (6,770 Touchdown / 5,737 Map2seq). Settings: Adam, lr 3e-4, batch 16, 20 epochs, greedy decoding, best checkpoint selected by dev TC.

VELMA-RBL: response-based/imitation training with λ=0.5 mix of teacher forcing and student forcing. In student forcing, a successful own trajectory (stop within one node of the goal) is used as the target; otherwise a shortest-path oracle provides stepwise corrective actions.

setting.backbone: LLaMA-7B (LoRA fine-tuned) for main VELMA-FT/RBL; frozen GPT-3 / GPT-4 / Mixtral for 2-shot variants. OpenCLIP ViT-bigG-14 (frozen) landmark scorer; GPT-3 landmark extractor
setting.model_size: 7B (LLaMA-7B for fine-tuned variants); few-shot variants use GPT-3/GPT-4 (closed) and Mixtral
setting.training_data: Touchdown (6,770) and Map2seq (5,737) training instances of the 'unseen' split (training area geographically separated from dev/test). Each is verbalized along the gold path, with landmark visibility from the CLIP scorer (no gold landmark annotations). RBL additionally uses on-policy rollouts with shortest-path oracle labels. Few-shot variants use only 2 in-context training examples.
setting.observation: Street View panorama cropped to five 60° FoV RGB views (−90°..+90°), converted to text via CLIP landmark detection, plus the number of outgoing edges (intersection type) at the current node
setting.action_space: discrete nav-graph actions: FORWARD / LEFT / RIGHT / TURN_AROUND / STOP (modified Touchdown graph)
setting.simulator: Touchdown Street View environment (lower Manhattan, 29,641 panoramas), modified by the authors
setting.privileged: none (intersection degree from the nav graph is part of the standard environment observation; CLIP scores are standardized with training-area panorama statistics)

numbers_note: Metrics are TC (task completion = success within one neighboring node, i.e. SR-like), SPD (shortest-path distance, lower is better) and KPA (key point accuracy). GPT/Mixtral few-shot variants were evaluated on dev only, citing cost and data leakage. Omitted to respect the variant cap: VELMA-GPT-3 dev results (Touchdown SPD 22.2 / KPA 49.1 / TC 6.8; Map2seq SPD 19.1 / KPA 58.1 / TC 9.2). The few-shot scaling results for OPT/LLaMA/LLaMA-2/Mistral are only in a figure (text quotes LLaMA-2 KPA 48.3/57.7 with TC 2.1/3.2). Vision ablation (Table 3, VELMA-FT dev): no image TC 15.0/37.8, CLIP ViT-L/14 20.8/39.2.
results: Fine-tuned VELMA-RBL (LLaMA-7B) sets a new state of the art on the unseen splits. Test TC is 26.4 on Touchdown and 47.5 on Map2seq, against 19.1/32.5 for ORAR♠-ResNet and 20.0/34.0 for ORAR♠-OpenCLIP, both retrained in the same modified environment. That is a 77%/57% relative gain over the originally reported ORAR (14.9/30.3). Few-shot VELMA-GPT-4 with only 2 in-context examples reaches 10.0/23.1 dev TC, i.e. 44%/77% of the fully trained ORAR♠-ResNet, while acting as a blind text-only agent.
limitations: Few-shot TC remains far below trained models. Only GPT-3/GPT-4/Mixtral achieve non-trivial TC, and closed GPT models were evaluated on dev only (cost / data-leakage concerns).

The verbalization bottleneck only checks instruction-extracted landmarks with a binary, hand-set CLIP threshold (τ=3.5) over 5 coarse directions. Detection errors (e.g. HSBC vs Bank of America) and missing spatial detail propagate directly to decisions.

Results use the authors' modified Touchdown environment (no auto-rotation, extra turn_around action) and the unseen split, so they are not directly comparable to numbers from the original environment.
